punchline: A forester scraped a mossy "stone" with his pocket knife and found green underneath: a stump alive centuries after it was felled.
thirty_sec: Forester Peter Wohlleben walked past some mossy stones for a long time. Then he scraped one with his pocket knife and found a green layer. The stones were the ring of an enormous beech stump, felled at least four hundred years earlier, and it was still alive. With no leaves of its own, he reasoned, neighbouring trees must be feeding it through their roots. Later reviews say some of this sharing is overstated. The book is The Hidden Life of Trees.
